REQUIREMENTS_ANALYSIS.EFFECTIVE_SPECIFICATION: Only ISSUE32 defines the target contract. Previous specifications are available in immutable Git history and Issue #25 approval discussions; they are not part of these active XML artifacts. No /v1, /v2, Bearer, legacy-client support or data migration.

ISSUE32_REQUIREMENTS_REVISION.SCOPE: Target-only correction. Historical approved clauses and approval records remain as evidence of prior decisions; incompatible historical API paths are not the target contract. No production implementation authorized.
ISSUE32_REQUIREMENTS_REVISION.GOAL: One unified direct/group conversation service exposed solely through the unversioned /conversations HTTP resource tree, authenticated exclusively with BFE Drive Internal Auth validated DPoP-bound sessions.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: All target conversation HTTP operations use /conversations and its unversioned descendants. /v1 and /v2 are not target HTTP APIs. Existing /v2 domain behavior is the implementation migration baseline, not a second API.

Every protected target HTTP request requires DPoP proof bound to the validated BFE Drive session through existing Internal Auth; plain Bearer is not an accepted authentication scheme. WebSocket authentication and subscriptions preserve required independent membership verification and revocation rules.
Direct and group conversations share one conversation identity, message stream, authorization model and history semantics, retaining type-specific membership and ownership rules.

Retain all functional direct/group conversation behavior, permissions, message/document handling and idempotency from the working /v2 implementation. No legacy-client support, production-data inventory or migration is in scope; destructive removal of populated legacy tables is not authorized.

A 1:1 conversation is created by authenticated account UUID and distinct peer UUID. Self-direct is rejected. Creation for the same unordered pair is unique and concurrency-safe. Personal hide affects only caller visibility, never peer access, messages or direct identity.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for direct without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Authenticated user creates named group with owner and selected account UUIDs. Maximum 100 members including owner. Creator is owner. Group supports rename, invited-member changes, role management and departure. A member may leave. The owner must transfer ownership to another current group member before leaving; if there is no other current member, the last owner cannot leave. Exactly one owner must remain after each successful operation.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for group without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Owner may manage group and appoint or dismiss admins, while preserving exactly one owner; admin can only perform explicitly allowed membership or rename operations, cannot remove owner/other admin, appoint admins or transfer ownership; member cannot administer group. BFE Drive ADMIN status does not grant Chat membership or management.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for roles without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Every membership addition/removal creates an auditable bounded visibility interval. Read and message delivery are permitted only for messages within caller intervals. On rejoin, messages from the gap stay hidden. Removal immediately blocks subsequent protected operations and active WebSocket subscriptions. Membership mutations and send/delivery authorization have a defined atomic ordering.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for membership without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Each conversation has one stable monotonic conversation-scoped message order and cursor pagination, default 50 and max 100 messages per page. Every history query filters by authenticated viewer membership intervals. The same visibility rule applies to reconnect and historical catch-up.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for history without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Only authenticated current members send messages; sender identity is never supplied by a trusted client field. Text maximum 16384 UTF-8 bytes, request JSON maximum 65536 bytes. Idempotency key replay returns original result for identical content and 409 Conflict for different content; concurrency cannot create duplicates.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for message without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Optional message context holds document ID and title; preserve both in message history and events. Chat neither copies document content nor grants any BFE Drive document rights. Document access is independently checked by BFE Drive.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for document without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Centrifuge publishes persisted messages only to currently authorized members. Revalidate authorized subscriptions and revocation even for established sockets. Reconnect recovers missed messages through persisted conversation history; multi-device membership and read states remain coherent.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for realtime without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Read marker is monotonically increasing per account and conversation and shared across devices. Unread counts include only authorized messages sent by other users. One member cannot advance another member read marker.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for read without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: All Chat-specific conversation state and ACLs are within bfe_chat. BFE Drive sessions are validated through existing Internal Auth UDS; account UUID alone grants no Chat authorization. Reject out-of-scope access without leaking data.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for isolation without changes to legacy clients or production data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Group names limited to 256 UTF-8 bytes; no more than 100 group members; JSON body max 65536 bytes; message text max 16384 UTF-8 bytes; history page max 100. Reject invalid input before changes or publications.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Verify authorized success, unauthorized rejection, concurrency or boundary behavior for limits without changes to legacy clients or production data.

ISSUE36_REQUIREMENTS_REVISION.SCOPE: Propose replacing Centrifuge with ntfy as the sole chat realtime notification transport. This proposal is not effective until Human Approval; the approved ISSUE32 baseline remains effective. This revision authorizes no implementation, dependency change, production configuration change, database operation, merge to the effective baseline, or deployment.
ISSUE36_REQUIREMENTS_REVISION.PROJECT_GOAL: Replace Centrifuge with ntfy for realtime wake-up notifications while preserving backend-authoritative history, authorization, membership visibility, sender exclusion, document privacy, and production safeguards.

PROPOSED_ACCEPTANCE_LIMITS.LIMIT: Maximum interval from authoritative session or membership revocation to termination of every active subscription and cessation of protected event delivery.
Maximum interval between reconciliation checks for an authenticated active client while the backend is reachable, including detection of silently lost ntfy signals.
PROPOSED_ACCEPTANCE_LIMITS.NOTE: These are explicit proposed values for Project Owner approval, not effective production guarantees. If rejected, the requirements must be revised before Human Approval; implementation may not choose substitute values silently.

ISSUE36_REQUIREMENTS_REVISION.ACTOR: Authenticated current conversation member other than the sender

USE_CASE.ACTION: Commits a chat message through the backend
USE_CASE.GOAL: Notify other currently authorized members that backend history may have changed without disclosing message or document data through ntfy

REQUIREMENT.RULE: ntfy replaces Centrifuge as the sole target chat realtime notification transport. The target must not retain Centrifuge as a parallel or fallback realtime transport. ntfy is only a wake-up/invalidation channel; PostgreSQL-backed backend state and authorized HTTP history remain the source of truth for messages, order, membership, and visibility.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: The approved target architecture and later runtime/dependency inventory identify ntfy as the only realtime notification transport and show no Centrifuge runtime path. A notification alone cannot return or authorize access to message data.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: The backend is the only authority for recipient selection, topic provisioning, publishing, and subscription authorization. Before issuing a subscription grant, the backend validates the caller's current BFE session through the existing Internal Auth/DPoP boundary and independently validates active conversation membership and its epoch. A grant is opaque, read-only, scoped to one recipient, one active session, one opaque per-membership-epoch topic, and one membership epoch; its lifetime is at most 30 seconds and its unique grant identifier may be consumed only once. Expired, replayed, cross-session, cross-account, cross-topic, or stale-epoch grants are rejected. DPoP proofs and BFE session credentials are not forwarded as ntfy credentials. Credentials must be transmitted in authorization headers or a server-side authenticated relay, never in URLs/query parameters, and must never be logged. Only the backend service identity may publish; clients cannot publish or select arbitrary recipients/topics. The concrete mechanism is selected in Technology only if it satisfies these properties; topic secrecy alone is not authorization.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Negative tests reject missing/invalid DPoP, expired/replayed grants, a grant used by another session/account, a grant scoped to another topic/epoch, anonymous access, client publishing, and arbitrary topic selection. Request captures and logs contain no credential, DPoP proof, or grant token in URL or log fields.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Authoritative logout, account switch, session expiry/revocation, membership removal, or membership-epoch change immediately blocks new publication to the revoked recipient/epoch. All already-open subscriptions for the revoked session/epoch must be terminated and protected event delivery must cease no later than the proposed 30-second revocation limit. The client must immediately clear prior-session chat state on logout/account switch and discard events associated with the old session. Rejoining creates a new membership epoch and a distinct topic; an old grant or topic cannot authorize the new epoch.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Timestamped tests for every listed revocation trigger prove no new publication after authoritative revocation, no protected event delivery after the approved maximum bound, immediate client-side state clearing on logout/account switch, and denial of the old epoch after rejoin. Tests explicitly distinguish events already received before revocation from delivery after the bound.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: The application notification envelope is versioned and contains an opaque random wakeToken unique to a recipient notification attempt; it contains no conversation, message, account, or document identifier. The client treats wakeToken as a deduplication/coalescing key, not a message cursor or proof of delivery. Client correctness must not depend on ntfy ordering, cache retention, replay limits, or delivery guarantees. Each client maintains the last successfully synchronized conversation ordinal using the existing authorized history cursor contract and reconciles on each notification, reconnect, app resume, and at least once every proposed 30 seconds while its session is active and the backend is reachable. Reconciliation requests history after the last cursor; backend authorization and membership-interval filtering are applied on every request. Duplicate, delayed, reordered, or silently lost signals must converge to the same authorized ordered backend history.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Tests drop a notification without closing the stream and prove the next scheduled reconciliation detects and fetches the missing history within the approved interval. Duplicate and reordered wakeToken values do not duplicate messages or alter order. Reconnect/resume catch-up returns all currently visible missing messages, respects membership intervals, and advances the cursor only after successful synchronization.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: The complete application-supplied ntfy publish request is allowlisted. The application message body contains exactly integer version and opaque random wakeToken. No application-supplied title, tags, priority, click URL, actions, attachment, sender identity, message text, document ID/title/content, account/conversation/message identifiers, access credential, or other application metadata is permitted. The ntfy topic is opaque and unpredictable and encodes none of those values. ntfy-generated transport fields are not application payload and must not be treated as authoritative. Document ID and title may remain in authorized backend message history and internal backend events where required by the existing message contract, but never in ntfy payload or metadata. Chat membership does not grant BFE Drive document access.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Capture the full publish request and verify the body has only version and wakeToken, the topic is opaque, no application-set metadata is present, and no protected data or credentials appear in ntfy requests or application logs. Verify authorized history still retains required document ID/title and Drive independently denies unauthorized document access.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Notification publication is best-effort and occurs only after durable message commit. A successful message commit remains successful if ntfy publication fails. Each notification attempt has a durable recorded outcome. An ambiguous/UNKNOWN publish outcome is not automatically retried, because the broker may already have accepted it; consumed attempts are not blindly replayed. Notification delivery may be permanently lost, but the client reconciliation contract in REQ36-RT-04 guarantees eventual history refresh within the approved interval whenever the authenticated client and backend are reachable. Failure or retry must never alter committed message state, bypass authorization, or emit protected payload.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Inject definite and ambiguous publication failures after commit. Verify the message remains persisted and readable by authorized members, attempt outcome is recorded, no consumed UNKNOWN attempt is replayed, no duplicate durable message is created, and an active reachable client obtains the committed message through scheduled reconciliation within the approved interval.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Every protected history/read request independently validates the current BFE session through Internal Auth/DPoP and current conversation membership/visibility interval. A notification or subscription grant does not authorize history access. Logout/account switch clears prior-session cache and subscription state before displaying data for the new session. Multi-device synchronization remains based on backend history and existing per-account read-state semantics.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: A revoked or switched session cannot read history even if it still possesses an old ntfy message or grant. Tests verify that prior-session cached messages are cleared before new-session content is displayed and history access is independently denied after revocation.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Chat membership, ntfy topic access, and notification receipt never grant BFE Drive document rights. Document open/download remains independently authorized by BFE Drive. The administrative UI is not a chat realtime subscriber unless a separate approved requirement explicitly adds that use case.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Chat membership and ntfy access alone cannot open/download a protected document. The architecture and subscriber inventory exclude the administrative UI from ntfy subscriptions.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: This proposal authorizes no implementation, dependency change, production configuration change, database migration, merge to the effective baseline, or deployment. Before implementation approval, the GRACE package must inventory all current Centrifuge call sites/dependencies and deployed consumers within this repository's authority, document compatibility and any required coordinated release outside this repository, and define rollout, observability, rollback, and the no-mixed-transport invariant. Production repositories and external client repositories are outside this change's authority and must not be modified by this process.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: The requirements-only PR changes no runtime source, dependencies, database, or production configuration. A later implementation gate includes an evidence-backed integration/consumer inventory, compatibility plan, rollout and rollback plan, and explicit approvals; no external repository is changed by this task.

REQUIREMENT.RULE: Web and Android behavior must be specified and verified for the explicitly supported browser/OS matrix before implementation. Web transport/authentication must work without credentials in URLs and must document CORS and header handling. Android must reconcile on process resume and connection recovery. No universal background-delivery guarantee is assumed; notification delivery may be delayed or unavailable under OS lifecycle restrictions. The specific supported matrix and compatible transport mechanism are Technology-stage decisions constrained by these requirements.
REQUIREMENT.ACCEPTANCE: Before implementation authorization, the Technology artifact names supported browser and Android versions and provides a verification matrix for transport, authorization, CORS, foreground/background, Doze, process death, force-stop, resume, and reconnect. Tests do not assert impossible OS-level background delivery guarantees.

ISSUE36_REQUIREMENTS_REVISION.INVARIANT: Only committed backend state and current backend authorization determine message visibility and access.
The sender is never an ntfy recipient for their own message.
The only application-supplied ntfy body fields are version and opaque wakeToken; no protected content, identifiers, credentials, or custom metadata are supplied.
A revoked session or membership epoch cannot authorize delivery or history access after the approved revocation bound; a rejoined membership uses a new epoch and topic.
ntfy publication failure cannot invalidate or remove a committed backend message.
While an authenticated client and backend are reachable, missing notification signals are detected by scheduled reconciliation within the approved maximum interval.

BUSINESS_PROCESS.STEP: A client submits a message through the existing authenticated backend API.
The backend validates session, membership, and visibility rules and durably commits the message.
The backend selects currently authorized recipients other than the sender and revalidates their membership epochs.
The backend creates one opaque, minimal wake-up envelope per recipient attempt and publishes only to that recipient's protected epoch topic; attempt outcome is recorded.
A recipient coalesces/deduplicates the signal and fetches authorized history from the backend using the existing ordinal cursor contract.
If a signal is lost or publication fails, scheduled reconciliation refreshes authorized history within the approved interval while the backend is reachable.
On logout, account switch, session revocation, removal, or rejoin, prior-session/epoch access is revoked within the approved bound and old client state is cleared as specified.
